claims.text: The initial material is bulk, coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy.
The proposed intervention combines laser shock peening with a calibrated mild heat pulse.
Pre-optimization by cyclic thermal-mechanical testing will ensure long-term stability of the engineered layer.
Laser shock peening combined with a mild heat pulse will create an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer in CoCrFeMnNi.
The treatment will create a nanohierarchical gradient microstructure containing nanocrystalline grains interspersed with nanoprecipitates.
The engineered near-surface layer will adapt structurally during wear.
Sliding shear and controlled tribo-oxidation will reorganize the pre-engineered layer into a self-lubricating glaze.
The glaze will minimize interfacial adhesion and adhesive wear.
The glaze will interrupt abrasive junction formation.
An ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer is associated with low friction and low wear in CoCrFeMnNi.
The treatment will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 30–40% relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The treatment will reduce wear rate by up to one order of magnitude relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The treatment will remain effective under continuous sliding from cryogenic temperatures to approximately 800 °C.
The treatment will remain effective in both ambient and inert environments.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi surfaces typically have higher friction coefficients and substantially higher wear rates under comparable conditions.
Extreme cyclic thermal-mechanical stresses may rapidly degrade the adaptive surface layer.
Highly corrosive atmospheres may limit the treatment's effectiveness.
The long-term integrity of the adaptive tribolayer across the full temperature range is uncertain under extreme cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.

contradictions.description: The mechanism requires controlled tribo-oxidation to produce a lubricating glaze, while the claimed operating envelope includes inert environments where oxidation may be strongly mitigated. No alternative glaze-forming route for inert operation is specified.
